before: list-style-type selects a marker such as square or decimal. list-style-position places it outside or inside the principal list-item box. Keeping a real ul or ol preserves the list structure while CSS adjusts its presentation.

Here square markers sit outside the text box. Start padding leaves room for them, and each li gets space after it. inside makes the marker part of the first line’s inline content, which can change wrapping. A decorative marker is not a substitute for meaningful item text. Logical spacing follows writing direction.

```html
  • Sketch the bank
  • Record the weather
``` ```css .tasks { list-style-type: square; list-style-position: outside; padding-inline-start: 24px; } .tasks li { margin-block-end: 10px; } ```

Keep a real unordered list, use square outside markers and add 10px space after each item. The supplied HTML stays in index.html; edit the CSS. The checks inspect this small page, not every possible browser or accessibility requirement.
after: A list marker is the symbol or number beside an item. `list-style-type` chooses its style. `square` requests square markers; `decimal` requests numbers.
`list-style-position: outside` keeps the marker outside the item’s main text box. `inside` puts it on the first line with the text, which can change how long items wrap.
Keep the real `ul` list and its `li` items. CSS changes how the markers look, not the list’s HTML meaning. Use an `ol` ordered list in HTML when the order itself matters.

before.question: Changing list-style-type from square to decimal changes what?
choices: The HTML list element automatically becomes ol.
The item text is replaced by numbers.
The marker style, not the ul element into an ol.
before.explanation: The CSS marker can look numbered, but it does not change the document’s element structure. Choose ol in HTML when order is meaningful.

after.question: What changes when list-style-type goes from square to decimal?
choices: The ul automatically becomes an ol.
The item words are replaced with numbers.
The markers change; the ul remains a ul.
after.explanation: CSS changes the marker’s appearance. It does not change the HTML element.
